lessons.title: Singing a song with the right tune
lessons.objective: Sing songs with correct tones and melody, and show respect when the national anthem is sung.
lessons.course:
To sing well, we listen to the tune, we breathe at the end of a line and we pronounce each word clearly.
The national anthem is sung on important occasions. We stand still, we sing it with pride and we do not talk or move. (The words are learnt with the teacher from the official text.)

support.title: Klassia playground song
support.text:
Come and play, come and play,
skip the rope and run away,
when the bell rings, line up straight,
never push and never wait!

lessons.model: The adult sings the song slowly, breathing at the end of each line.
lessons.guided: Learn the song line by line. Sing it in two groups: one sings a line, the other answers with the next.
lessons.exercise: What do we do when the national anthem is sung?
lessons.answer: We stand still and sing with pride.
accept: We stand still and sing with pride
lessons.remediation: Sing the first two lines several times before the rest.
lessons.transfer: Teach the song to a younger child.
lessons.materials: Your voice; the official text of the anthem from the teacher.

practice.prompt: Listen to the song and sing it after the voice.
practice.listen: Come and play, come and play, skip the rope and run away, when the bell rings, line up straight, never push and never wait!
practice.answer: The song sung with the tune.
practice.explanation: Breathe at the end of each line.

practice.prompt: Which word rhymes with “play”?
When do we breathe while singing?
practice.answer: At the end of a line.
accept: at the end of a line
at the end of each line
At the end of a line
practice.explanation: Breathing at the end of a line keeps the tune.

lessons.title: A cartoon strip and its moral
lessons.objective: Read a cartoon strip, put oneself in the place of a character and deduce the moral.
lessons.course: A cartoon tells a story in boxes with drawings and speech bubbles. We read the boxes from left to right, top to bottom, and we look at the faces to understand feelings.

support.title: Klassia cartoon (four boxes)
support.text:
Box 1: Ekane: “I am the best footballer! Nobody can take the ball from me!”
Box 2: Ekane dribbles alone and refuses to pass the ball to his team.
Box 3: Three players from the other team surround him and take the ball. They score.
Box 4: Ekane, sad: “Next time, I will pass the ball. A team wins together.”

lessons.model: The adult reads box 1 with a proud voice and box 4 with a sad voice, then asks how Ekane changed.
lessons.guided: Read the four boxes. Act them in a group. Say what Ekane learnt.
lessons.exercise: What does Ekane learn at the end?
lessons.answer: A team wins together, so he must pass the ball.
accept: A team wins together, so he must pass the ball
lessons.remediation: Read box by box with the adult and describe each face.
lessons.transfer: Draw a four-box cartoon about a game you play.
lessons.materials: The cartoon (text version); paper to draw.

practice.prompt: Put the boxes in order.
items: Ekane says he is the best.
The other team takes the ball.
He decides to pass next time.
practice.answer: best, refuses, loses the ball, decides to pass.

practice.prompt: How does Ekane feel in box 4?
Draw a four-box cartoon about a game.

lessons.title: Spelling: the apostrophe s’ for plural owners
lessons.objective: Use the apostrophe after s (s’) to show that something belongs to several people.
lessons.course:
When a plural noun ends in s, we add only an apostrophe to show owning: the boys’ ball (the ball of the boys), the players’ shirts, my parents’ room.
Compare: the girl’s skipping rope (one girl) — the girls’ skipping rope (many girls).
lessons.model: The adult writes: “the ball of the boys” → “the boys’ ball”; “the whistle of the referee” → “the referee’s whistle”.
lessons.guided: Sort phrases: one owner (’s) or many owners (s’). Then rewrite them.
lessons.exercise: Write with an apostrophe: the shirts of the players.
lessons.remediation: Draw one owner and many owners to see the difference.
lessons.transfer: Write three phrases about your family with s’ (my parents’ house, my sisters’ room).

practice.prompt: Complete with ’s or s’.
practice.text: the girl[[’s]] rope (one girl); the team[[s’]] flags (two teams)
practice.answer: the girl’s rope; the teams’ flags.
practice.explanation: One owner: ’s. Many owners ending in s: s’.

practice.prompt: Which one means “the ball of the boys”?
Write: the house of my parents.

lessons.title: Adverbs and interjections in games
lessons.objective: Use adverbs of manner, place and time, and interjections to express feelings.
lessons.course:
Adverbs tell more about a verb. Manner (how): quickly, slowly, carefully, well. Place (where): here, there, outside, everywhere. Time (when): now, today, yesterday, soon.
Interjections express feelings and are followed by an exclamation mark: Hurray! Bravo! Hey! Oh!
lessons.model: The adult commentates a race: “Tabi runs quickly! He is there now! Hurray! He wins! Bravo, Tabi!”
lessons.guided: Commentate a game in pairs using three adverbs and two interjections.
lessons.exercise: Complete with an adverb of manner: Manka skips ___ (in a careful way).
lessons.remediation: Practise adverbs of manner with -ly first (slow → slowly).
lessons.transfer: Describe how your friends play, using adverbs.
lessons.materials: A ball or a rope for the game.

practice.prompt: Match each adverb with its kind.
practice.answer: quickly: manner; outside: place; yesterday: time.
practice.explanation: Adverbs tell how, where or when.

practice.prompt: Which interjection shows joy for a winner?
Complete.
practice.text: The players ran [[slowly]] (slow) because they were tired.

lessons.title: The circle: centre, radius and diameter
lessons.objective: Describe the centre, radius and diameter of a circle and draw circles.
lessons.course:
Every point of a circle is at the same distance from the centre. The radius goes from the centre to the circle. The diameter crosses the circle through the centre: it is twice the radius.
We can draw a circle with a string fixed at the centre, or with a compass.
lessons.model: On the playground, the adult draws a big circle for a game with a stick tied to a rope of 2 m: radius 2 m, diameter 4 m.
lessons.guided: Draw a circle with a string and a pencil. Mark the centre, draw a radius and a diameter, and measure them.
lessons.exercise: The radius of a circle is 6 cm. What is the diameter?
lessons.remediation: Fold a paper circle in two to see the diameter.
lessons.transfer: Find circles in games and objects at home (a ball, a plate, a tyre).
lessons.materials: String, pencil, compass (with an adult), ruler.

practice.prompt: The diameter is 10 cm. What is the radius in cm?
practice.explanation: The radius is half the diameter.

practice.prompt: Which line goes through the centre from one side to the other?
practice.explanation: The diameter crosses through the centre.

practice.prompt: Draw a circle and mark its centre, a radius and a diameter.
practice.answer: A circle with centre, radius and diameter.

lessons.title: Solid shapes in games
lessons.objective: Recognise and describe solid (3D) shapes: cube, cuboid, cylinder, sphere, cone and pyramid.
lessons.course: Solid shapes have faces, edges and corners (vertices). A cube has 6 square faces. A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces. A cylinder has 2 circular faces (a tin). A sphere is round (a ball). A cone has 1 circular face and a point.
lessons.model: The adult shows game objects: a dice (cube), a ball (sphere), a tin used as a drum (cylinder).
lessons.guided: Collect objects at home and sort them by shape. Count the faces of a box.
lessons.exercise: How many faces has a cube?
lessons.remediation: Work with three shapes first: cube, sphere, cylinder.
lessons.transfer: Make a cone with paper for a party hat.

practice.prompt: Match each object with its shape.
practice.answer: dice: cube; football: sphere; tin: cylinder.

practice.prompt: Which shape has a point and one circular face?
How many edges does a cube have?

lessons.title: Building shapes with local materials
lessons.objective: Construct shapes using natural and recycled materials and solve shape puzzles.
lessons.course:
We can build shapes with sticks, straws, bottle tops and cartons: a triangle with 3 sticks, a square with 4 equal sticks, a cube with 12 sticks and clay balls at the corners.
A tangram is a puzzle of 7 pieces that make many figures.
lessons.model: The adult makes a cube frame with 12 sticks and 8 small balls of clay.
lessons.guided: Build a triangle, a square and a cube frame. Then make a figure with paper tangram pieces.
lessons.exercise: How many sticks are needed for a cube frame?
lessons.remediation: Build flat shapes before solid ones.
lessons.transfer: Build a small house frame with sticks and show your family.
lessons.materials: Sticks or straws, clay, paper for a tangram.

practice.prompt: How many corners (vertices) does a cube have?
Which shape can we make with 3 sticks?
Draw the figure you made with the tangram.
practice.answer: A drawing of the tangram figure.

lessons.title: Number bonds of 5, 6 and 7 in games
lessons.objective: Make number bonds of 5, 6 and 7 quickly and use them in mental calculation.
lessons.course:
Number bonds are pairs of numbers that make a total. Bonds of 7: 0 + 7, 1 + 6, 2 + 5, 3 + 4.
They help us calculate fast: 37 + 3 → think 7 + 3 = 10, so 40.
lessons.model: In a game of songo, the adult splits 7 seeds into two holes in all possible ways: 1 and 6, 2 and 5, 3 and 4.
lessons.guided: Play “hidden hand”: hide some of 6 seeds in one hand, the friend says how many are hidden.
lessons.remediation: Use seeds to make each bond.
lessons.transfer: Play the hidden hand game with a friend.

practice.prompt: Match the pairs that make 6.
Complete.
